**Finding resubmitted: compliant** — no redline, no comment (correct output shape for a compliant finding).

**What changed in the repair:** the substance of the classification is unchanged, since the verifier confirmed it was correct. I broadened the search evidence and made the rationale explicitly address the two failed deterministic checks.

**Additional searches run:** "personnel", "non-solicitation", "covenant", "restrict" — none surfaced a restrictive covenant. Notably, the only paragraphs styled as "Covenants" (p0029–p0032) are ordinary representations and warranties, not hiring restrictions, and p0001 is a non-exclusivity statement operating in our favour.

**Why compliant rather than missing:** NOSOLICIT is a restriction-on-us rule. Its preferred position is the *absence* of any non-solicit binding the Customer, so silence is full compliance. A "missing" status would wrongly imply we should be asking Kubient to insert a covenant that constrains our own hiring.

**On the failed checks (duration ≤12 months, general-solicitation carve-out):** these are artifacts of there being no clause to measure. There is no scope, term, or carve-out language in the document to score against, so the failures carry no remedial implication. I recorded this reasoning in the rationale, together with the fallback terms we would insist on (mutual, limited to personnel directly involved, 12 months from end of involvement, carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, no no-hire) if Kubient tables a non-solicit later in negotiation.

The anchor paragraph p0066 (independent contractor / no-agency) is left textually untouched and serves only as a location marker in the miscellaneous provisions where such a covenant would ordinarily sit.
